definitions.explanation: The color between red and yellow, named after the daidai (bitter orange) fruit. One of the traditional Japanese color names.

examples.japanese: {夕焼|ゆうや}けが{橙色|だいだいいろ}に{染|そ}まった。
{橙色|だいだいいろ}のセーターを{買|か}った。
{紅葉|こうよう}の{季節|きせつ}になると、{山|やま}が{橙色|だいだいいろ}や{赤|あか}に{色|いろ}づく。
examples.english: When autumn foliage season arrives, the mountains turn orange and red.

notes:
Named after {橙|だいだい}, the bitter orange (Citrus aurantium), a citrus fruit traditionally used in New Year decorations. {橙色|だいだいいろ} is the native Japanese word for the color orange.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {橙色|だいだいいろ}に{染|そ}まる: to be dyed/tinged orange
- {橙色|だいだいいろ}の{光|ひかり}: orange light
- {橙色|だいだいいろ}の{花|はな}: orange flower

SIMILAR WORDS:
- オレンジ{色|いろ}: orange — the loanword version, more commonly used in everyday conversation
- {橙色|だいだいいろ}: the traditional Japanese term, used in formal or literary contexts and in art

CULTURAL NOTE:
{橙色|だいだいいろ} is one of the seven colors of the rainbow in Japanese ({虹|にじ}の{七色|なないろ}). The {橙|だいだい} fruit itself is an auspicious symbol placed on top of {鏡餅|かがみもち} during New Year because its name is a homophone for {代々|だいだい} (generation after generation).
